description: Three realistic prompts run against a synthetic fixture instance, with the skill (CLI) and without it (raw HTTP plus a hand-crafted Anchor), plus a real-agent layer and a Playwright browser review. Results live in results/iteration-2/.

evals.name: read-feedback
evals.prompt: I'm reviewing feedback left on the fixture project's README.md. List the annotations on README.md and tell me what the human wants me to change. Don't change anything yet.
evals.expected_output: A parsed annotation list whose two threads carry the human's anchored spans and requests. The real-agent run additionally writes a short synthesized answer.
expectations: The list output parses as a JSON array (deterministic layer)
Both seeded human annotations are returned (deterministic layer)
Every note exposes author alice and isAgent false (deterministic layer)
The two requests are distinct threads with the expected anchored spans (deterministic layer)
Agent run: the answer names the Node 18 requirement and the placeholder-sentence request
Agent run: the answer synthesizes rather than echoing both note bodies verbatim
evals.baseline_notes: Raw HTTP can read this too; these reading assertions are non-discriminating by design. The agent-run answer check is non-tautological.

evals.name: create-from-quote
evals.prompt: Create an annotation on README.md quoting 'fox jumps' and saying: 'Explain what the fox represents; this is a placeholder.' Use your author name claude.
evals.expected_output: An annotation whose first note is author claude, isAgent true, and whose Anchor is Active — the stored blockText is the rendered paragraph ('The quick brownfox jumps overthe lazy dog.'), not the raw wrapped source line.
expectations: The create response parses as JSON with an annotation id
The created note carries author claude and isAgent true
The stored anchor references the requested span
The stored anchor equals the CLI builder (structural)
Hard-wrapped prose projects to rendered text (soft breaks concatenate)
The stored anchor resolves Active through the real frontend resolver (rendered blocks + resolveAnchor)
Oracle control: a raw-line whole-block anchor resolves Outdated in the same run
Agent run: a real claude -p session creates an Active annotation with author claude
evals.baseline_notes: The no-skill baseline posts a whole-block anchor whose blockText is the raw source line; the server accepts it, but the real resolver returns Outdated.

evals.name: resolve-author
evals.prompt: Resolve every annotation authored by claude in the fixture project, then confirm none remain unresolved. Leave the human's annotations alone.
evals.expected_output: Both claude-authored annotations resolved, no unresolved claude threads left, and the alice-authored thread still unresolved.
expectations: The author filter returns only threads containing a claude note
Batch resolve updates exactly the claude annotations
Annotations from other authors stay unresolved
evals.baseline_notes: Raw HTTP can do this too; the assertions confirm the documented ?author= contract.
